known_gap: F-0008 (master session's finding, 2026-10-21). The product has no check that compares a part's pin-to-net map against the DESIGN INTENT. On this board the check that could reach the second source ACTUALLY RAN and still passed: IV.2 compared D1's pinout against the KiCad symbol for 1N4148W-7-F, agreed (T1), and reported '3 part(s) agree with an independent transcription'. The diode is fitted backwards and the board is emitted for fabrication. This is the same gap as F-S0-0001 / F-0007 on the swapped_pins case, but on a board where the second source RESOLVES, so the gap cannot be blamed on a missing symbol lookup.
expected_detector: NONE TODAY — this is a named false pass
description: D1, the 1N4148W-7-F flyback diode in SOD-123, is fitted the wrong way round. The design puts the anode on SW_LOAD and the cathode on VCC_5V, so the diode is reverse biased in steady state (4.8 V across it with the anode 4.8 V below the cathode) and conducts only while the load's inductance collapses, clamping SW_LOAD to about -0.7 V and keeping the flyback pulse off Q1's collector. The defect puts the anode on VCC_5V and the cathode on SW_LOAD. The diode now conducts in the steady state it was supposed to block: with Q1 on, the rail is shorted to the load through the diode at 4.8 V forward bias, five times a 1N4148W's 0.7 V drop, so the load sees the full rail, Q1 switches nothing, and the diode itself is destroyed by the sustained current. And when Q1 turns off, the cathode is on the load side, so the diode BLOCKS the flyback it was built to clamp, putting the inductive spike onto Q1's collector. The part that exists to protect the transistor destroys it.
seed_target: D1's pins in the netlist, which name the diode's terminals by FUNCTION: base {A: SW_LOAD, K: VCC_5V} becomes {A: VCC_5V, K: SW_LOAD}. On the board the same transposition appears in pad space, because SOD-123 puts the cathode on pad 1 and the anode on pad 2 (footprints.PINMAPS, KiCad and JEDEC convention): base {1: VCC_5V, 2: SW_LOAD} becomes {1: SW_LOAD, 2: VCC_5V}. The base board is the REAL product output, not a fixture — the load_switch generator runs on a 30 mA inductive load, PcbNetlistGenerator translates the CircuitIR into the netlist the PCB engine consumes, and compile_board routes it. The defective board is recompiled from the defective netlist by the same product path, so the copper and the pad map both carry the fault.
notes: THIS CASE IS A NAMED FALSE PASS AS OF 2026-10-21, and that is the finding, not a gap in the seed. The product's own verifier returns ok=True and the gate says {emit: true, reason: '6 check(s) unproven (unknown rung)'} on the defective board. NOTHING flips: no check changes status between the base board and the defective one. THE STRONG FORM OF THE FINDING: unlike the swapped_pins case, the second source is fully reachable here. part_pinouts.lookup('1N4148W-7-F', 'SOD-123') resolves by prefix to KiCad's Diode:1N4148W, whose symbol says pad 1 = K and pad 2 = A. IV.2 therefore ACTUALLY RUNS on D1 and reports '3 part(s) agree with an independent transcription (T1)' — on a board whose diode is backwards. Why it passes: IV.2 asks whether the NET on pad N agrees with what the SYMBOL says pad N is. It resolves the netlist's function name 'A' through the symbol to pad 2 and 'K' to pad 1, then checks that pad 2 carries the net the netlist calls 'A'. On the defective board that is all still true — the board faithfully realises the defective netlist. What changed is WHICH NET each terminal is on, and a symbol describes a part's terminals, not what a particular design must connect them to. A datasheet pinout table answers 'which terminal is the cathode'; only the CIRCUIT answers 'which net belongs on the cathode'. The gap is architectural rather than a missing rule: compile_board calls verify_board(board, netlist) with the SAME netlist it just compiled from, so the verifier can only ever answer 'is this board what I was told to build', never 'is what I was told to build right'. The product's own path confirms this: the defective board verified against the defective netlist has zero failed checks. THE FIX NEEDS TWO THINGS, not one: a source of truth for the DESIGN INTENT that survives into the verifier (the CircuitIR, or a polarity rule the generator states and the verifier re-derives), and a check that reads a diode's polarity against it. Closing the symbol lookup alone would NOT close this case.
